Russians work three shifts to build jet-powered missiles powered by a $16,000 Chinese engine from AliExpress
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-08-12
16:50:50 UTC
01:50:50 KST

Russia is turning out its cheap Banderol drone-cruise missile at scale. Russia is capable of producing up to 80 jet-powered weapons a month, Ukraine's Defense Intelligence (HUR) told the defense outlet Militarnyi in response to a query.
The production figure sharpens a threat Ukraine has tracked as the Banderol expands. The missile has a relatively short range of about 500 kilometers, so Russia effectively launches it from Crimea at Odesa. It means Russia can sustain and grow the Banderol strikes on Ukraine's south, a weapon whose ground launcher Ukraine recently found could let Russia fire it without warning and in salvos.
The missile is fast, cheap, and short-range
The Banderol was developed and is made by the Russian company Kronshtadt, reaching a maximum speed of 620 to 650 kilometers per hour and cruising at 520 to 560, with a fragmentation-high-explosive warhead of 114.3 kilograms, of which 49.5 kilograms is explosive.
Its range dictates where it is used. At about 500 kilometers, the Banderol cannot reach far into Ukraine, which is why Russia fires it from occupied Crimea at Odesa, using the peninsula's proximity to strike the southern port city that has borne so much of Russia's missile campaign.
It has launched them at the Kyiv agglomeration to hit Rozetka, Ukraine's largest online retailer.
Banderol's jet propulsion allows speeds that Ukrainian mobile fire teams cannot match with standard ground-based machine guns. Countering the missile requires systems like the Gepard that can track fast-moving targets.
The production runs on Western parts
The 80-a-month figure comes at a cost in effort and imports. To sustain the stated production rate, Russian enterprises work in three shifts, and to make the missiles, Russia uses Western components.
Ukraine's War & Sanctions portal documented over 20 foreign-made components and approximately 20 microchips of foreign origin from 30 different companies in the missile's construction, with a Chinese Swiwin SW800Pro jet engine, available on AliExpress for approximately $16,000, powering the weapon.

Latvia has discovered its first known border tunnel used to enter the country illegally from Belarus, the country’s State Border Guard said on 11 August. Officers intercepted 15 people who had crossed through the underground passage and returned them to Belarus.
Latvia, Lithuania, and Poland accuse Belarus and Russia of directing migrants toward their borders to retaliate for EU sanctions and strain countries supporting Ukraine. Minsk and Moscow deny orchestrating the crossings. Tunnels found in Lithuania and Latvia show organizers adapting to fortified borders, requiring Baltic governments to deploy more personnel and surveillance technology.
The tunnel was about 10 meters from Latvia's fence
Border guards found the group on 10 August in Skrudaliena parish, in Latvia’s southeastern Augšdaugava municipality, and briefed the public on the discovery the following day. The operation involved the State Police, a Lithuanian border-service dog handler, and a rapid-response unit, the Latvian Border Guard said.
While reconstructing the group’s route, officers found the passage near the Silene border post, about 10 meters from Latvia’s fence. The agency said it had received intelligence that a tunnel might be under construction, but had previously found no sign of a breach there.
Riga answered on 11 August 2026 by launching Operation Vilkatis, or “Werewolf,” scheduled to run through the end of August. The government says the operation will improve intelligence-sharing among border guards, police, the military, and security services. It will also expand aerial surveillance and target networks that transport and shelter migrants after they cross.
The Belarusian tunnel to the EU was almost done. Then Lithuania drilled a hole in exactly the wrong place—for the diggers
Latvia faced 87% of all crossing attempts along the EU-Belarus border by mid-July 2026
Belarus has weaponized migration since 2021, when EU governments accused Alyaksandr Lukashenka’s regime of bringing people from the Middle East and Africa to the bloc’s frontier in retaliation for sanctions. Belarus denied orchestrating the crisis.
Latvia reported more direct evidence in January 2026. Documents and phones taken from detained migrants linked Belarusian military and border personnel to organized crossings, according to Latvia’s armed forces and Border Guard.
By 13 July, Latvia had recorded 7,791 attempts over 111 consecutive days, 87% of all attempts along the EU-Belarus border by then. Lithuania later found an unfinished tunnel dug from Belarus. Latvia’s tunnel, unlike the unfinished Lithuanian passage, had already been used.

That is why we insist that the No. 1 priority for return should be severely wounded and seriously ill citizens of Ukraine. But Russia returned to us the bodies of those whom it could still have returned alive

Ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe: death toll rises to 44

Ferry capsizes on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe: death toll rises to 44
Kyiv • UNN
An overcrowded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, killing at least 44 people. The vessel was designed to carry 90 people, but there were more than 100 passengers on board.
At least 44 people were killed after an overloaded ferry capsized on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe. The Guardian reported this, citing police, according to UNN.
Details
The vessel was designed to carry 90 people, but 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unknown number of children were on board, Zimbabwe’s Civil Protection Unit (CPU) said earlier on Wednesday, citing ticket sales data.
One crew member told national broadcaster ZBC that there were 153 people on board when the ferry capsized on Tuesday after hitting large waves. A passenger told ZBC that the vessel began taking on water approximately 30 minutes after leaving the lakeside town of Kariba, heading toward islands and fishing camps.
A specialized team of underwater rescuers was dispatched to the site, the CPU said, and search-and-rescue operations continued on Wednesday. At that point, the CPU reported that the death toll stood at 15, with another 27 people missing.
A boat sank on Lake Kariba in Zimbabwe, killing at least 15 people12.08.26, 12:38 • 2620 views
On Wednesday afternoon, Zimbabwean police updated the death toll twice within 32 minutes in posts on the X platform. The first post said that 38 people had died, adding: "Bodies have been retrieved from the lake." It was then reported that 44 deaths had been confirmed so far.
Video published by ZBC on Tuesday showed several people sitting on the overturned ferry while at least four speedboats came to their aid and a helicopter circled overhead.
In addition
Lake Kariba is the world’s largest artificial lake by volume of water, stretching approximately 150 miles along Zimbabwe’s northern border with Zambia. It was created in the 1950s during British colonial rule, when the Zambezi River was dammed, forcing approximately 57,000 people to leave their homes. The Kariba Dam supplies at least one-third of the electricity of both countries.
Boat capsizings on the lake are not uncommon. In 2014, 26 people, 24 of them children, drowned in the Zambian section of the lake when a boat carrying them to Independence Day celebrations capsized.
On the Zimbabwean side, five people drowned in 2021, and another three are believed to have died in October 2023. A month earlier, a police boat capsized, although no one was killed.
